parts:
Hey Dr Karl and everyone,
I used effectplot function to plot the phenotypes and get the usual graph but the resolution of the figure (including the lines and labels) was too faint. I tried to use, cex.axis and cex.lab arguments but were invalid. My question is how to obtain better graph for a paper .
Thank you for your reply
Bothaina Hassan

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: effectplot function
parts:
The effectplot function doesn't allow a lot of customization.
So your best bet is probably to save the R code for the function to a file and edit it to suit your needs.

    dput(effectplot, "myeffectplot.R")

will save it to a file. Add  "myeffectplot <- " at the top, and then edit the code to do what you want.

Use source("myeffectplot.R") to make the new function available to you.

karl
